newsitem.title: USA: U.S. carmakers urge Clinton, Hashimoto talks on yen.
newsitem.headline: U.S. carmakers urge Clinton, Hashimoto talks on yen.

text.p: U.S. automobile makers said Friday they would like President Clinton and Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto to discuss the weak yen, which they said was behind "disturbing" car trade trends.

"The excessive depreciation of the yen against the dollar is a serious problem which is reversing some of the hard-won gains made in correcting the bilateral U.S.-Japan trade imbalance," American Automobile Manufacturers Association President Andrew Card said in a statement.

"We hope that Mr. Hashimoto, who previously served as Japan's trade minister and chief auto negotiator, will address the current disturbing trends in the bilateral automotive trade imbalance, as well as the recent U.S. government review of the 1995 U.S.-Japan auto agreement," he said.
He noted a lack of progress in getting more dealers in Japan to sell U.S.-made cars and in deregulating Japan's highly-regulated car parts market.

Separately, some 28 member of the House of Representatives and 25 senators signed letters to Clinton urging him to discuss access to Japan's film and photographic paper markets. A U.S. complaint against Japan on the trade dispute is pending at the World Trade Organization.
Clinton and Hashimoto were to hold formal discussions at the White House today.
